description: Pre-build xfce-winxp-tc RPMs as OCI artifacts, consume them in the image build, track upstream commits with Renovate, and add smoke-test CI.

userStories.title: Centralize xfce-winxp-tc version in a single env file
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the xfce-winxp-tc commit hash defined in exactly one file so that Renovate and all build scripts share a single source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: File `xfce-winxp-tc.env` exists at the repo root containing `XFCE_WINXP_TC_VERSION=<commit-hash>`
`files/scripts/20-xfce-winxp-tc.sh` no longer hard-codes the version; it sources `xfce-winxp-tc.env` or reads the variable from it
`files/scripts/packages/xfce-winxp-tc/justfile` no longer hard-codes the version; it reads from `xfce-winxp-tc.env`
No other file in the repo contains a hard-coded xfce-winxp-tc commit hash
shellcheck passes on all modified shell scripts
userStories.notes: Current hash is 4f73e4a740041635eecd30abccc2fdafabb21582 — copy it into xfce-winxp-tc.env as the starting value. The justfile uses Just syntax; reading an env file from Just requires a `set dotenv-load` or `dotenv-filename` directive — check Just docs for the right approach.

userStories.title: GitHub Actions workflow to build xfce-winxp-tc RPMs and publish as OCI artifact
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a CI workflow that builds xfce-winxp-tc RPMs inside a container and publishes them to GHCR as an OCI artifact, so the image build no longer needs to compile from source.
acceptanceCriteria: New file `.github/workflows/build-packages.yml` exists
Workflow triggers on: `workflow_dispatch`, push or PR that modifies `xfce-winxp-tc.env` or the workflow file itself
Workflow reads `XFCE_WINXP_TC_VERSION` from `xfce-winxp-tc.env` using a shell step
Workflow builds RPMs using the existing `files/scripts/packages/xfce-winxp-tc/Containerfile` (containerized build with Podman or Docker)
Resulting RPMs are pushed to `ghcr.io/winblues/xfce-winxp-tc-rpms:<version>` using `oras` CLI
On PR events, the artifact tag is `pr-<PR-number>` instead of the commit hash, to avoid overwriting release artifacts
Workflow fails if the RPM output directory is empty after the build
Workflow authenticates to GHCR using `GITHUB_TOKEN` (packages: write permission)
YAML is syntactically valid (use `yamllint` or GitHub's own YAML parser — no syntax errors)
userStories.notes: oras CLI docs: https://oras.land/docs/. Use `oras push ghcr.io/winblues/xfce-winxp-tc-rpms:<tag> --artifact-type application/vnd.bluexp.rpms <rpms-dir>/`. The existing Containerfile is at files/scripts/packages/xfce-winxp-tc/Containerfile. The build inside the container runs `bash /app/packaging/buildall.sh` from the xfce-winxp-tc source root. RPMs land in xptc/*/rpm/std/x86_64/fre/. Check the existing justfile at files/scripts/packages/xfce-winxp-tc/justfile for the exact build steps to replicate in CI.

userStories.title: Update image build script to install RPMs from OCI artifact
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the image build to pull pre-built RPMs from the GHCR OCI artifact and install them, eliminating the source compilation step from the image build.
acceptanceCriteria: `files/scripts/20-xfce-winxp-tc.sh` no longer clones or compiles xfce-winxp-tc from source
Script pulls the OCI artifact from `ghcr.io/winblues/xfce-winxp-tc-rpms:<version>` using `oras pull`
`oras` is installed in the script's environment via `dnf5 install -y oras-cli` (or equivalent package name on Fedora)
Script installs the downloaded RPMs with `rpm-ostree install`

Script sources `XFCE_WINXP_TC_VERSION` from `xfce-winxp-tc.env` (the file must be available in the build context — add it to the `files` module in `recipes/recipe.yml` if needed, or copy it in the script)
Script exits non-zero immediately if `oras pull` fails (no silent fallback to source build)
Build dependencies (`cmake`, `gcc-g++`, etc. from `build-deps.txt`) are no longer installed by this script
Plymouth theme is still set to `bootvid` after RPM installation
shellcheck passes on the modified script
userStories.notes: The file xfce-winxp-tc.env needs to be accessible inside the container build. BlueBuild copies the files/ directory into the build context, but xfce-winxp-tc.env is at the repo root. Options: (1) move it to files/scripts/xfce-winxp-tc.env and reference it from there, (2) add it to files/ so BlueBuild copies it, or (3) embed the version lookup differently. The simplest approach may be to place xfce-winxp-tc.env inside files/ so it gets copied by the files module. Coordinate with US-001 — wherever the file lands, all references must agree.

userStories.title: Configure Renovate to track xfce-winxp-tc upstream commits
userStories.description: As a developer, I want Renovate to automatically detect new commits on the xfce-winxp-tc default branch and open a PR to update the hash in `xfce-winxp-tc.env`, so version bumps require no manual work.
acceptanceCriteria: `renovate.json` exists at the repo root with valid Renovate configuration
Configuration includes a `customManagers` entry using `regex` manager that matches `XFCE_WINXP_TC_VERSION=<hash>` in `xfce-winxp-tc.env`
The datasource is `git-refs` pointing to `https://github.com/rozniak/xfce-winxp-tc` tracking the default branch (upstream has no tags, only commits)
Renovate PR title follows the pattern: `chore(deps): update xfce-winxp-tc to <new-hash>`
GitHub Actions dependency updates are preserved (either keep `.github/dependabot.yml` or migrate them into `renovate.json` — do not lose them)
`renovate.json` is valid JSON (no parse errors)
The `renovate.json` includes `"$schema"` pointing to the Renovate config schema URL for editor validation
userStories.notes: Renovate git-refs datasource docs: https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/git-refs/. The customManagers regex approach: use `fileMatch` targeting xfce-winxp-tc.env, `matchStrings` to capture the hash, `depNameTemplate` for the dep name, `datasourceTemplate: git-refs`, `packageNameTemplate: https://github.com/rozniak/xfce-winxp-tc`. Existing dependabot config is at .github/dependabot.yml — read it first and decide whether to migrate or keep both.

userStories.title: Create smoke test script that boots the image in QEMU and verifies system health
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a script that boots the built bootc image in a QEMU VM and confirms the system reaches a healthy state, so I can verify images are not broken locally or in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Script `scripts/smoke-test.sh` exists and is executable
Script accepts one argument: a container image reference (e.g. `ghcr.io/winblues/bluexp:latest`)
Script uses `bootc-image-builder` via Podman to convert the container image to a QCOW2 in a temp directory, using `config.toml` or a test-specific config with a known SSH keypair
Script boots the QCOW2 with QEMU using port-forwarding (host port 2222 → guest port 22)
Script polls SSH on port 2222 until the system is reachable, with a 5-minute timeout; if timeout is exceeded, script exits non-zero
On successful SSH connection, script runs `systemctl is-system-running` and accepts `running` or `degraded` (fails on `failed` or `starting` after timeout)
On successful SSH connection, script checks `systemctl is-active lightdm` returns `active`
QEMU process is killed on script exit regardless of pass/fail (use a trap)
Temp directory (QCOW2) is cleaned up on exit
Script prints clear PASS or FAIL with reason to stdout
Script exits 0 on pass, non-zero on failure
`just test-smoke` recipe exists in `justfile` that calls `scripts/smoke-test.sh` with the locally built image reference
shellcheck passes on `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
userStories.notes: bootc-image-builder Podman invocation example is already in the justfile (`just vm` recipe) — reuse that pattern. For the SSH keypair: generate a throwaway ed25519 keypair in the script (or check in a test fixture key at scripts/smoke-test-key) and inject it via a test-specific config-test.toml. The QEMU command needs: -m 4096 -smp 2 -drive file=<qcow2>,format=qcow2 -netdev user,id=net0,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=net0 -nographic. SSH polling: use `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 -i <key> -p 2222 user@localhost true` in a loop.

userStories.title: Add package build job to CI that runs before image build
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the CI pipeline to automatically build and publish the xfce-winxp-tc OCI artifact before building the image, so that Renovate PRs (and any PR changing xfce-winxp-tc.env) are tested end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: `.github/workflows/build.yml` is updated to include a `build-packages` job that runs `build-packages.yml` (via `workflow_call`) or duplicates the essential steps inline
The `build-image` job declares `needs: build-packages` so it waits for packages to be published before starting
If `xfce-winxp-tc.env` has NOT changed in the PR/push, the `build-packages` job is skipped and the image build uses the already-published OCI artifact tagged with the current `XFCE_WINXP_TC_VERSION`
If `xfce-winxp-tc.env` HAS changed, the `build-packages` job runs and publishes the new OCI artifact before the image build starts
The condition logic uses `git diff` or GitHub's `paths` filter to detect changes to `xfce-winxp-tc.env`
YAML is syntactically valid
userStories.notes: Two approaches for conditional job: (1) Use a separate `check-changes` job that outputs whether xfce-winxp-tc.env changed, then use `if: needs.check-changes.outputs.changed == 'true'` on the build-packages job. (2) Use `workflow_call` on build-packages.yml and call it from build.yml. Approach (1) is simpler for a single repo. To make build-packages.yml reusable via workflow_call, add a `workflow_call` trigger to it. The build-image job should always run regardless of whether packages were rebuilt.

userStories.title: Add smoke test job to CI pipeline that runs after image build
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the CI pipeline to automatically run the smoke test after every image build, so broken images are caught before they are merged or published.
acceptanceCriteria: `.github/workflows/build.yml` includes a `smoke-test` job that runs after `build-image` (`needs: build-image`)
Smoke test job runs on all PRs and pushes (not just version-bump PRs)
Smoke test job installs prerequisites: `oras`, `qemu-system-x86`, `bootc-image-builder` (via Podman, already available on ubuntu-latest)
Smoke test job pulls the PR image (tagged `pr-<number>` on PRs, or the branch image on push) and passes it to `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
Smoke test job has a 15-minute job-level timeout (`timeout-minutes: 15`)
If the smoke test fails, the workflow run is marked failed and the PR cannot be merged (assuming branch protection is configured)
QEMU/KVM access is enabled on the runner via the standard `sudo chmod 666 /dev/kvm` setup step (required on ubuntu-latest)
YAML is syntactically valid
userStories.notes: ubuntu-latest runners support KVM — other projects confirm this works. Enable it with: `- run: sudo chmod 666 /dev/kvm` before invoking QEMU. The image reference for PRs from the BlueBuild action is typically `ghcr.io/winblues/bluexp:pr-<number>` — verify the exact tag format the blue-build/github-action produces by reading its docs or output. The smoke-test.sh script (US-005) must exist before this story can be implemented.
